# Robinhood Chain — Colosseum resource index

Every link below is copied verbatim from Colosseum's published corpus, including its curator caveats.

### Start here

**Core resources**

- [Robinhood Chain developer documentation](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/)
  - Official entry point for the permissionless EVM Layer 2, with routes to network, contract, asset, bridge, oracle, and operations documentation.
- [Connect to Robinhood Chain](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/connecting/)
  - Copy the official mainnet and testnet chain IDs, public RPCs, explorers, sequencer feeds, and wallet configuration; public endpoints are rate-limited and not for production.
- [Robinhood Chain testnet faucet](https://faucet.testnet.chain.robinhood.com/)
  - Request 0.01 testnet ETH and five of each listed Stock Token once every 24 hours. Faucet eligibility and actual claim execution remain untested.
- [Differences from Ethereum](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/differences-from-ethereum/)
  - Required reading for Nitro block semantics, fee accounting, address aliasing, finality, transaction ordering and screening, and the 96 KB contract-size limit.
- [Deploy smart contracts](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/deploy-smart-contracts/)
  - Deploy and verify Solidity contracts with Foundry or Hardhat, using testnet first and Blockscout for source verification.
- [Robinhood Chain status](https://status.robinhoodchain.offchain.io/)
  - Check mainnet and testnet service health and upgrade notices before treating an RPC, feed, or sequencer issue as an application bug.

### Verify network activity

**Network explorers**

- [Robinhood Chain mainnet explorer](https://robinhoodchain.blockscout.com/)
  - Inspect and verify mainnet contracts, transactions, addresses, blocks, and logs on the official Blockscout instance.
- [Robinhood Chain testnet explorer](https://explorer.testnet.chain.robinhood.com/)
  - Inspect testnet activity and verified contracts; the homepage exposed stale placeholder-looking summary data during review, while its API and the testnet RPC returned current blocks.

### Build with Stock Tokens

**Token and pricing references**

- [Building with Stock Tokens](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/building-with-stock-tokens/)
  - Learn the ERC-20 and ERC-8056 multiplier model, balance presentation, integration patterns, and permissioned primary mint and redemption boundary.
- [Robinhood Chain token contracts](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/contracts/)
  - Use Robinhood's live contract registry for WETH, USDG, and Stock Token addresses instead of copying addresses from examples.
- [Stock Token APIs](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/stock-token-apis/)
  - Read the public asset, raw underlying price, and corporate-action REST endpoints; prices differ from multiplier-adjusted onchain token feeds and the service is rate-limited.
- [Robinhood Chain oracles and price feeds](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/oracles-and-price-feeds/)
  - Implement AggregatorV3 reads with decimals, heartbeat staleness, L2 sequencer uptime, multiplier, and oracle-pause checks.
- [Chainlink Robinhood tokenized-equity feeds](https://docs.chain.link/data-feeds/tokenized-equity-feeds/robinhood)
  - Review the oracle provider's source-of-truth model for total-return values, 24/5 sessions, corporate-action pauses, staleness, and integration risk.

### Cross-chain and account integrations

**Integration guides**

- [Bridge assets](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/bridging/)
  - Compare the canonical Ethereum bridge with third-party routes; canonical withdrawals take about seven days and token availability varies by route.
- [Account abstraction](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/account-abstraction/)
  - Integrate ERC-4337 or EIP-7702 with documented provider examples; hosted bundlers and paymasters can require accounts, API keys, quotas, or payment.
- [Cross-chain messaging](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/cross-chain-messaging/)
  - Register the custom network with the Arbitrum SDK and handle retryable tickets, address aliasing, and the seven-day L2-to-L1 challenge period.

### Operations and reference code

**Advanced references**

- [Robinhood Chain dapp reference](https://github.com/hummusonrails/robinhood-chain-dapp-example)
  - Inspect an Arbitrum Foundation-featured Foundry, Next.js, viem, and wagmi Stock Token sample with local, testnet, mainnet, and mainnet-fork paths; it is reference code, not evidence of a deployed production app.
- [Run a Robinhood Chain full node](https://docs.robinhood.com/chain/run-a-full-node/)
  - Start from Robinhood's node entry point, then follow current Arbitrum Nitro requirements and use the Robinhood chain configuration; expect substantial memory, storage, and parent-chain RPC needs.
